translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty was founded he retired as senior general and returned to Yong.

sentences.zh: 未久，思綰過雍，遂閉門據雍城叛，衣冠之族，遭塗炭者眾，公全家免禍。

translations.literal: Before long Siwan passed through Yong, shut the gates, seized Yong city and rebelled; many of the gentry families suffered ruin, but the lord's whole household escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Siwan passed through Yong, shut the gates, and rebelled from the city. Many gentry families were ruined, but the Li household escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 終以計勸思綰納款，遂拔雍城。）〉

translations.literal: In the end, by stratagem he persuaded Siwan to submit, and Yong city was taken.)〉
translations.idiomatic: In the end he persuaded Siwan to surrender by stratagem, and Yong was recovered.)〉

sentences.zh: 思綰然之，即令讓能為章表，遣牙將劉成琦入朝。

translations.literal: Siwan agreed; he at once had Rangneng draft the memorial and sent junior officer Liu Chengqi to court.
translations.idiomatic: Siwan agreed, had Rangneng draft a memorial, and sent junior officer Liu Chengqi to court.

sentences.zh: 制授思綰華州留後、檢校太保，以常彥卿為虢州刺史，遣內臣賫官告國信賜之。

translations.literal: By decree he was appointed acting prefect of Hua Prefecture and acting Grand Guardian; Chang Yanqing was made prefect of Guo Prefecture, and an inner court official was sent bearing commission documents and imperial credentials to bestow them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him acting prefect of Huazhou and acting Grand Guardian, made Chang Yanqing prefect of Guozhou, and sent a palace official with commissions and imperial credentials.

sentences.zh: 既受命，遲留未發。

translations.literal: After receiving the appointment he delayed and did not set out.
translations.idiomatic: After accepting the appointment he lingered and would not depart.

sentences.zh: 郭從義、王峻等籌之曰：「狼子野心，終不可用，留之必貽後悔耳！」

translations.literal: Guo Congyi, Wang Jun, and others deliberated, saying, "A wolf cub has the heart of a wolf—he can never be used; if we keep him we are sure to regret it later!"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Congyi and Wang Jun debated the matter. "A wolf cub will always be a wolf," they said. "He can never be trusted. Keep him and we will regret it."

sentences.zh: 既而從義、王峻等緩轡入城，陳列步騎至牙署，遣人召思綰曰：「太保登途，不暇出祖，對飲一杯，便申仳別。」

translations.literal: Before long Congyi, Wang Jun, and the others entered the city at an easy pace, arrayed foot and horse troops at the headquarters, and sent men to summon Siwan, saying, "The Grand Guardian is on the road and has no time for a full farewell banquet—let us drink one cup together and then take our leave."
translations.idiomatic: Congyi and Wang Jun then entered the city at an easy pace, drew up infantry and cavalry at headquarters, and summoned Siwan with the message, "The Grand Guardian is departing and has no time for a full farewell—share one cup with us and we part."

sentences.zh: 思綰至，則執之，遂斬於市，並族其家。

translations.literal: When Siwan arrived they seized him, beheaded him in the market, and executed his whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Siwan came they seized him, executed him in the market, and exterminated his clan.

sentences.zh: 〈（《東都事略·郭從義傳》云：思綰困甚，從義遣人誘之，佯許以華州節鉞。

translations.literal: (Eastern Capital Historical Outline, biography of Guo Congyi: Siwan was in desperate straits; Congyi sent men to entice him and falsely promised him the military governorship of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: (Eastern Capital Historical Outline, biography of Guo Congyi: Siwan was desperate. Congyi sent envoys to lure him with a false promise of the Huazhou command.

sentences.zh: 思綰信之，遂開門送款，從義入城，思綰謁見，即遣武士執之。）〉

translations.literal: Siwan believed it, opened the gates and offered submission; Congyi entered the city, Siwan came to audience, and he at once sent warriors to seize him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Siwan believed him, opened the gates, and submitted. Congyi entered the city; when Siwan came to audience, warriors seized him at once.)〉

sentences.zh: 思綰臨刑，市人爭投瓦石以擊之，軍吏不能禁。

translations.literal: As Siwan faced execution the townspeople vied to throw tiles and stones at him; military officers could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: At his execution the townspeople hurled tiles and stones at him until the guards could not hold them back.

sentences.zh: 是日，並部下叛黨新授虢州刺史常彥卿等五百餘人並誅之。

translations.literal: That same day, together with more than five hundred rebel followers under him, including the newly appointed prefect of Guo Prefecture Chang Yanqing, all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: That day more than five hundred of his followers, including the newly appointed prefect of Guozhou Chang Yanqing, were executed with him.

sentences.zh: 籍思綰家財，得二十餘萬貫，入於官。

translations.literal: Siwan's family property was registered; more than two hundred thousand strings were obtained and entered into government coffers.
translations.idiomatic: His property was inventoried at more than two hundred thousand strings, all seized for the state.

sentences.zh: 始思綰入城，丁口僅十餘萬，及開城，惟餘萬人而已，其餓殍之數可知矣。

translations.literal: When Siwan first entered the city the registered population was only a little more than a hundred thousand; when the city was opened, only about ten thousand remained—the number who starved to death can be imagined.
translations.idiomatic: When Siwan seized the city it had a registered population of barely a hundred thousand. When the gates were opened again, only about ten thousand remained—the toll of starvation speaks for itself.
